Orders, credit and dispatch your dealers can see without calling.

For brands that sell through distributors and dealers, and for distributors serving retailers and contractors, in building materials, electricals, paints, lubricants, agri inputs and industrial supplies. We digitize dealer ordering, connect it to credit and dispatch data, and give field teams a simple way to plan beats and report visits.

What makes distributors & dealer networks different

  • Dealer orders arrive as WhatsApp texts, photos and calls that the order desk re-types into Tally or the ERP.

  • Reps book orders for dealers who are over their credit limit because exposure is visible only to accounts.

  • Dealers call sales to ask for dispatch, transporter and e-way bill details on almost every consignment.

  • Visit reports, competitor activity and dealer complaints stay in rep chats instead of the CRM, so coverage gaps go unseen.

Where automation helps distributors & dealer networks

  • WhatsApp or portal ordering

    Registered dealers order through a WhatsApp Flow or a simple portal, validated against their price list, schemes, pack sizes and stock before the order desk releases it.

  • Credit checks and ledger-based reminders

    Show limit, overdue and hold status when an order is placed, send statements and reminders to the dealer's nominated accounts contact, and route scheme or short-supply disputes to the right owner.

  • Dispatch and e-way bill updates

    Share invoice, e-way bill number, transporter, vehicle and LR details automatically once goods leave the warehouse, and capture proof of delivery.

  • Beat plans and voice-note visit reports

    Suggest weekly beats from sales, overdue and last-visit data, and turn reps' WhatsApp voice notes into structured CRM visit records they confirm.

  • Warranty claims and spare requests through dealers

    Dealers log customer warranty claims and spare-part requests with serial numbers and photos, and see status without calling the service team.

  • Principal and supplier PO follow-ups

    Follow up open POs with principals and suppliers, read revised dates from their replies, and flag backorders to the dealers affected.

Order & credit checkStandard4–6 weeks

Dealer and distributor ordering on WhatsApp or a portal

Let registered dealers place orders on WhatsApp or a simple portal, validated against the ERP price list, schemes, pack sizes, stock and credit position before a draft sales order reaches the order desk.

Distributors & dealer networks

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Dealers send orders as WhatsApp texts, photos of handwritten lists and calls to the sales rep. The order desk re-types them into Tally or the ERP, confirms stock and schemes by phone and discovers credit holds only after the order is entered. Orders get missed in the month-end rush, SKU codes are misread, and dealers have no confirmation of what was actually booked.

Trigger

A dealer whose WhatsApp number is mapped to a customer code sends an order message or completes a WhatsApp Flow, or submits a cart on the dealer portal.

How it runs

  1. Identify the dealer from the registered number or portal login and load their price list, schemes and usual SKUs from the ERP or Tally through its API or a scheduled sync.
  2. Read the order from the WhatsApp Flow, portal cart or free text, map items to SKU codes and pack sizes, and ask the dealer to confirm any line the system is unsure about.
  3. Check stock or available-to-promise by warehouse, minimum order and scheme eligibility, and show partial availability or approved substitutes.
  4. Check the dealer's credit limit and overdue balance from the receivables feed and flag the order for hold if limits are crossed.
  5. Create a draft sales order in the ERP or order queue for the order desk, and send an approved confirmation template with the order reference once it is released.

Human checkpoint

The order desk releases every order with an exception: unclear SKUs, price or scheme overrides, stock shortfalls or credit flags. Orders on credit hold are released only by the credit controller. Prices and schemes always come from the ERP, never from the AI.

Payment & collectionsStandard3–5 weeks

Credit-limit checks and overdue payment reminders

Compute each dealer's exposure against their credit limit every day, flag orders for hold, and send courteous ledger-based reminders before and after due dates, with escalation to the rep and then the credit controller.

Distributors & dealer networks

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Receivables live in Tally or the ERP, but credit decisions happen in conversations. Reps keep booking orders for dealers who are over their limit, reminders depend on whoever has time, and disputes about schemes, credit notes or short supply surface only when a payment is already late. Month-end becomes a round of phone calls.

Trigger

A nightly receivables and aging export from the ERP, a new order from a dealer, or an invoice reaching an agreed reminder point before or after its due date.

How it runs

  1. Pull outstanding invoices, credit notes, receipts and aging per dealer from Tally or the ERP and reconcile totals with the accounts team's ledger.
  2. Calculate exposure against the approved credit limit and payment terms, and mark each dealer as clear, watch or hold.
  3. Send approved WhatsApp utility templates or emails about the dealer's own account, with a ledger statement, to the nominated accounts contact at agreed points around the due date.
  4. Capture replies such as payment made, promise to pay or dispute, and route disputes about schemes, credit notes or short supply to the right owner.
  5. Escalate unresolved overdues to the rep, then to the credit controller, and send finance a weekly collections summary.

Human checkpoint

The credit controller decides credit limits, holds, releases, extensions and any legal step. Reminders use approved, non-threatening wording, and an open dispute pauses reminders for that invoice until a person resolves it.

Invoice, dispatch & deliverStandard3–5 weeks

Dispatch updates with invoice, e-way bill and documents

When an order is invoiced and dispatched, send the buyer the invoice, e-way bill number, transporter and vehicle details, plus the CoA and safety data sheet where needed, and alert the dispatch team before an e-way bill expires in transit.

Distributors & dealer networks · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Buyers and dealers call the sales rep to ask whether goods have left, which transporter is carrying them and when they will arrive. Dispatch teams forward invoice photos on WhatsApp, certificates of analysis are emailed separately, and e-way bills sometimes lapse on delayed consignments because nobody is watching validity.

Trigger

The ERP marks an invoice as posted with an IRN and e-way bill number, or the transporter updates the lorry receipt or vehicle number.

How it runs

  1. Read invoice number, IRN status, e-way bill number and validity, transporter, vehicle number and LR details from the ERP or GSP integration.
  2. Check for gaps such as missing Part B vehicle details, values that differ between invoice and e-way bill, or missing batch documents, and alert dispatch before the truck leaves.
  3. Attach the invoice and, for chemical and pharma shipments, the batch certificate of analysis released by QC and, for hazardous products, the current safety data sheet from the regulatory or EHS owner.
  4. Send an approved dispatch template to the buyer's opted-in contacts with document links and the expected delivery window.
  5. Watch e-way bill validity against transit status, alert the dispatch lead and transporter before the extension window opens, and capture proof of delivery from the transporter.

Human checkpoint

The dispatch lead handles every exception; vehicle changes and e-way bill extensions are made in the e-way bill system by the dispatch team or the transporter carrying the goods. The automation never generates, cancels or extends e-invoices or e-way bills; it reads status and alerts people. Only QC releases CoAs.

Service, field visits & reorderStandard4–6 weeks

Sales rep beat planning and visit reporting

Plan weekly dealer and retailer beats from sales, overdue and stock data, then let reps report each visit as a short WhatsApp voice note or form that becomes a structured CRM record and a daily summary for managers.

Distributors & dealer networks

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Field reps plan visits from memory, return to the same easy dealers and report the day as a long WhatsApp message to their manager. Competitor activity, display issues, stock gaps and complaints stay in chats instead of the CRM, so head office cannot see coverage or follow up on what dealers asked for.

Trigger

A weekly planning run on Monday morning, and each visit check-in or voice note a rep sends from the field.

How it runs

  1. Suggest a weekly beat per rep from dealer sales trends, overdue status, last visit date and open complaints, for the area manager to adjust and approve.
  2. Let the rep check in at a visit and send a voice note or short form on WhatsApp or the CRM app.
  3. Transcribe the note and extract order intent, stock gaps, competitor activity, complaints and promised actions into structured fields for the rep to confirm.
  4. Create follow-up tasks for orders, service requests or scheme queries and assign them to the right team.
  5. Send managers a daily coverage summary and a weekly view of planned versus completed visits.

Human checkpoint

Area managers approve beat plans and review exceptions. Reps confirm each extracted visit record before it is saved. The system reports planned and completed visits only; any decision about a rep's performance rests with their manager, using fuller context.

Service, field visits & reorderAdvanced6–8 weeks

Service, AMC and warranty tickets with spare-part requests

Log service requests with machine serial number, photos and symptoms, check warranty or AMC status, assign the right engineer, suggest checks from approved manuals and turn spare-part needs into stock checks or quotes.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Distributors & dealer networks

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Customers and dealers report breakdowns by calling whoever they know. Service coordinators look up warranty and AMC status in spreadsheets, engineers travel without the right spare or manual, and parts quotes for out-of-warranty machines take days. AMC renewals lapse because nobody tracks expiry dates.

Trigger

A customer or dealer raises a request on WhatsApp, the portal or by email, or an AMC visit or renewal date comes due.

How it runs

  1. Capture the machine serial number, site, symptoms, error codes and photos through a guided WhatsApp or portal form.
  2. Check the serial number against the installed base, warranty terms and AMC contract, and show the machine's service history.
  3. Suggest likely causes and checks for the engineer from approved manuals and past tickets, with links to the source pages.
  4. Assign an engineer by territory, skill and availability, start SLA timers and update the customer with approved templates.
  5. For parts, check stock and raise a warranty replacement request or an out-of-warranty quote for approval; remind customers of AMC renewals and preventive visits.
  6. Close the ticket with the engineer's report, parts used and customer sign-off.

Human checkpoint

The service engineer diagnoses and decides the repair, and the service manager approves warranty acceptance or rejection and any goodwill. Faults involving guarding, interlocks, pressure or electrical hazards go straight to an engineer; the assistant never advises bypassing a safety device.

Plan, procure, make & checkStarter2–4 weeks

Supplier PO follow-ups and inbound material tracking

Follow up open purchase orders before their due dates, read supplier replies into expected dates for the buyer to confirm, and flag shortages against the production plan or dealer backorders.

Distributors & dealer networks · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Buyers chase suppliers and principals by phone and email for every open PO. Revised dates stay in inboxes, planning learns about a packaging or raw material shortage on the day of production, and distributors discover a principal's short supply only when dealers complain.

Trigger

An open PO line approaches its due date, a supplier replies to a follow-up, or a goods receipt differs from the PO.

How it runs

  1. Read open PO lines, due dates and supplier contacts from the ERP every morning.
  2. Send templated follow-up emails before and on the due date from the buyer's mailbox or a shared purchase address.
  3. Use AI to read supplier replies for committed dates, partial quantities and issues, and propose updated expected dates for the buyer to confirm.
  4. Compare expected receipts with the production plan or dealer backorders and flag shortages to planning or sales.
  5. Flag goods receipt mismatches, and alert accounts as invoices from registered micro or small suppliers near the MSMED Act payment deadline, which cannot exceed 45 days from acceptance.

Human checkpoint

The buyer confirms every revised date before it reaches planning. Changes to PO price, quantity or supplier are made only by the purchase manager in the ERP. Shortfalls of client-supplied material are raised with the brand client by the account manager.
